html:
SMTO-LLM-0054 — The AI model ended its reply in a way SMTO doesn't recognize

GUID: 393881e8-1cbf-4494-b3af-9d85db4249c1
Slug: model-finish-reason-invalid
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: llm

What happened

  • The model's reply ended with a signal SMTO can't read, so SMTO couldn't tell whether the reply was complete. Nothing from that reply was run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look at the steps already shown for this task and check which ones actually finished; don't assume the task is done. The unreadable end signal says nothing about whether the task's work was completed.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing and pick a different model for Main (and Helper, if one is set), then save. The odd end signal comes from the model server, so another model or server usually avoids it.
  3. If someone else runs your AI model server, tell them its replies end with an unreadable finish reason. They can correct how the server reports the end of each reply.
  4. Send a new message asking SMTO to continue from where it stopped, without repeating the steps that already finished. SMTO can then finish any remaining work based on what you saw had already been done.

What success looks like

  • SMTO's next reply completes normally and the task shows its remaining steps finishing.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages your AI model server. You don't need to shorten or clear the conversation; this problem isn't caused by its length.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The response's finish_reason is present but not a string, so normalization rejected the turn before dispatch; a malformed finish reason does not establish that the task or any operation completed.

What this means

  • The finish marker has an unsupported type or meaning at response normalization; it cannot by itself establish that the task or an operation completed. This category concerns model preparation or response acceptance. It does not reverse earlier operations or establish their outcome; their receipts remain authoritative.

Why this can happen

  • The finish marker has an unsupported type or meaning at response normalization; it cannot by itself establish that the task or an operation completed.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the provider's finish-reason mapping separately from retained operation receipts and task-completion state.

How to fix it

  • Inspect choices[0].finish_reason in the raw response from the configured endpoint; it must be a string such as 'stop', 'tool_calls' or 'length'. Correct the serving stack's finish-reason mapping or route to a compatible endpoint. A malformed finish reason does not establish task completion.
  • Inspect the model serving stack’s finish-reason mapping and restore the negotiated protocol. A malformed finish reason does not establish task completion.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported finish marker agrees with the returned content and passes the full envelope validator.

What not to do

  • Do not replay prior successful operations to repair a later model response.
  • Do not disable protocol validation or treat this representation failure as input-context overflow.

Technical notes

  • This category concerns model preparation or response acceptance. It does not reverse earlier operations or establish their outcome; their receipts remain authoritative.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
